brief: A group of local painters that are part of the painters union that were here to do some work with the hospitals or one of the other big  projects, said, Hey, we wouldn't work on that. There has been a lot of interracial work that's been done in that  regard, especially since the black population has never been above 3% in the history of Duluth. The AME church motto is to it's  administered to the spiritual, social and physical needs of the community. That's and then we take and then the garden also takes that fresh produce and members of the church and local  communities, deliver that fresh produce to folks who may not live close by the church, but still need that fresh produce.

file: Housing Segregation and Redlining in America: A Short History | Code Switch | NPR
brief: Many of those suburbs institute rules called covenants  that explicitly forbade selling homes to black people,  and all of this was perfectly legal. Well, the discrimination in housing is the major reason  that black families, up and down the income scale,  have a tiny fraction of the family wealth that white families do,  even white families with less education and lower incomes. It means that people have a lot of unnecessary contact  with the criminal justice system just because of where they live. Blue meant good people like white collar families,  yellow meant a declining area with working-class families,  and red meant detrimental influences.
